item: Row 387: the erase walks go by the data folder's handle
summary: On POSIX the walks of 5b and step 6, the top-level listings and the removal start from the handle the erase took on the data folder before its first write: every folder opened by name from it with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY, every file looked at, written and unlinked by name through its folder's handle; the folder itself removed only while its path still leads to that very folder. A drive or folder swapped mid-walk is never reached by its path (a by-path control test shows the old walk reaching it). A folder on no marked drive gets the same handle. Windows keeps the walk by path, the window stated in SECURITY.md. Security reads (three pairs): refused database copies stay kept by their name as the walk spells it, never by identity; salt-gone databases by the file's identity; a folder on another device below is never entered or emptied (the removal is the app's own iterative walk by handle, never shutil.rmtree); a data folder moved or swapped mid-erase is emptied through its handle and reported folder_moved, never removed; a handle that cannot be taken names the folder as not checked; a POSIX fallback to path walks is logged.
